title: Single Number
statement:
Given a non-empty array of integers `nums`, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one.

You must implement a solution with a linear runtime complexity and use only constant extra space.
constraints:
- `1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4`
- `-3 * 10^4 <= nums[i] <= 3 * 10^4`
- Each element in the array appears twice except for one element which appears only once.
hints: XOR of a number with itself is 0.
XOR all numbers; pairs cancel out, leaving the single number.

title: Number of 1 Bits
statement: Write a function that takes the binary representation of a positive integer and returns the number of set bits it has (also known as the Hamming weight).

examples.explanation: The input binary string 1011 has a total of three set bits.
The binary string 10000000 has one set bit.

hints: n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit.
Repeat until n is 0, counting iterations.

title: Reverse Bits
statement:
Reverse bits of a given 32 bits unsigned integer.

Note that in some languages, such as Java, there is no unsigned integer type. In this case, both input and output will be given as a signed integer type. They should not affect your implementation, as the integer's internal binary representation is the same, whether it is signed or unsigned.
constraints: - The input must be a binary string of length 32.

examples.explanation: The input binary string represents the unsigned integer 43261596. The reversed binary string represents 964176192.

hints: Process each bit from LSB to MSB, build result from MSB to LSB.
